text:
morgan: Heads up — did a quick post-deploy sweep on the new kernel selection heuristics and noticed KV cache bootstrap behavior changed. KV hit-rate for chat prompts dropped from ~78% -> ~63% during the first 10m after deploy. p95 tail up ~12ms. link to perf dashboard: https://internal.redwood/perf/runs/27777 :eyes:

sasha: ugh. timeline? was that the kernel roll that landed at 10:07am?

morgan: yes landed at 10:07. we swapped the attention kernel selector to prefer the reduced-buffer kernels for short sequences, which improved steady-state throughput but seems to change request ordering and KV key normalization in the preprocessor path.

jay: key normalization? thought the preproc wasn't touched. what changed exactly?

morgan: subtle change — when the kernel path decided to truncate trailing whitespace for the reduced-buffer fast-path, the canonicalization step now sometimes drops a trailing newline that we previously kept. that altered cache keys for ~17% of prefixes we see in canary traffic. hence lower warmup overlap.

elaine: that explains the hit shift. can you paste the profiler dump for a deploy window?

morgan: pasted snippet from profiler (10:07–10:17):
```
KV_PREFIX_HITRATE: baseline 0.78 -> post-deploy 0.63
TOP_PREFIXES_TARGETED: 120k -> 118k (same cardinality)
KEY_COLLISIONS_DETECTED: 0.04% -> 0.07%
BATCHING_EFFECTIVE_LATENCY: 8ms -> 9.8ms
CPU_SYS_KERNEL_SELECTOR: +6%
```

rachel: interesting that collisions rose slightly. maybe hashing + normalization mismatch. we should avoid changing canonicalization as part of kernel selection — it's mixing concerns.

jay: agreed, but we also need to consider warmup strategy changes. our deploy-time priming (what we call the "bootstrapper") currently fires 30s after route becomes healthy with 500 synthetic short prompts. if canonicalization shifts, those synthetic prompts won't match production traffic keys.

morgan: proposal: two changes — (1) separate the canonicalization from kernel heuristic decision so the key path is stable across kernel swaps; (2) introduce a staged bootstrapper: a micro-ping pass immediately on deploy for top-1k prefixes (fast, high QPS for 15s) + a slow drip job that runs every 5m for 30m to backfill lower-frequency prefixes.

elaine: +1 on stable keying. for (2) can we make the micro-ping use live sampling of traffic hot prefixes rather than static top-k? that would handle sudden motif changes after deploy.

morgan: yes — plan is micro-ping pulls from recent-5m hot-prefixes in the routing cache and pings only exact canonical keys. sample curl payload for the synthetic generator: 
```
POST /synthetic/ping
{ "prefixes": ["How do I reset my password?", "Summarize:", "Translate to Spanish:"], "mode": "exact-canonical", "burst_qps": 800, "duration_s": 15 }
```

infra-bot: deploy 27777 succeeded in us-west-2 on van-rt-12 at 10:07:03 (canary=3/3, green)

jay: need to watch autoscale interaction. when ASG ups a node, our current autoscale handler doesn't run bootstrapper automatically for the new node — we rely on the central scheduled job. so scale spikes (e.g., sudden RPS) will create cold capacity with no prefix warm.

sasha: can we piggyback on the scale-up lifecycle hook to trigger a per-node micro-bootstrap? tiny TTL so it doesn't run for scale churn. maybe only if expected dwell > 3m.

morgan: yes lifecycle hook firing micro-bootstrap (sampled). also add a cooldown flag: skip if node started by a rolling deploy (we already have separate deploy bootstraps).

rachel: metrics to monitor after changes: deploy 10m hit-rate delta, p95 latency delta, synthetic-match-rate (what fraction of synthetic pings hit the runtime prefix cache vs cold). also a regression detector: if hit-rate drops >8% post-deploy, auto-roll previous kernel and open an oncall incident.

elaine: +1. also log the canonicalization diff vector per deploy — small SHA of canonicalization mapping so we can quickly see if mapping changed between releases.

morgan: I'll open a PR to: (a) decouple canonicalization, (b) add micro-bootstrapper implementation (pull hot-prefix sample), (c) lifecycle hook micro-bootstrap, (d) metrics and alert. planning to run a blue/green with the micro-bootstrap enabled on blue only.

jay: one more thought — batching heuristics: the reduced-buffer kernel changed request sequencing which impacted batching coalescing. might be worth tuning continuous-batcher to favor intra-tenancy coalescing for first 30s post-node-start to preserve hit-rate.

morgan: good call. add config toggle: batch.coalesce_window_ms_post_start = 40ms (default 8ms). we'll test impact on throughput vs hit-rate.

sasha: love this. TL;DR action items?

morgan: TL;DR:
- PR: preserve canonicalization independent of kernel, add canonical-sha to deploy logs (morgan)
- PR: micro-bootstrapper (hot-prefix sampling) + curl API for synth generator (morgan)
- Infra: lifecycle-hook micro-bootstrap on ASG scale-up (sasha)
- Runtime: batch.coalesce_window_ms_post_start toggle & experiment (jay)
- Observability: metrics, alert, dashboard for deploy delta (rachel)

deploy-bot: noted — will annotate deploys with canonical-sha when present

elaine: I'll pair-review the canonicalization PR this afternoon. thanks for the quick triage :thumbsup:

morgan: thanks all — will follow up with the PR links and a canary run plan.

rachel: when you run the canary, add a small A/B for synthetic ping strategy: static top-k vs live-hot sample. want to see which backfills better.

morgan: will do. scheduling canary for 2pm PT. if anyone wants to join the runbook review ping me.
